intent: Give the Sarathi apex seat governed memory recall. Before this change `grep -c memory_kernel` over dharma_swarm/holon_system/sarathi/*.py returned 0 on every file, while CLAUDE.md names MemoryKernel the canonical front door for agent memory: she planned every wake cycle from the backlog alone, with no recall. New organ sarathi/memory.py reads through MemoryKernel.preview_memory_pack and only that front door, under a tight apex budget (no projections, no high canon/PII risk, references not payloads, reject_stale). Wired end to end -- daemon -> BootPack.memory_excerpt -> wake -> operator brief -- because a declared but unpopulated field is decoration: BootPack.lodestone_excerpt was declared and then appeared exactly once in the whole repo, its own declaration. Two negative controls in tests/test_sarathi_memory.py guard the producer and the consumer, both verified to FAIL when the wiring is removed.

commit.message: feat(sarathi): give the apex seat governed memory recall

honest_blockers: active_track is a SERVING claim, not an ownership claim. No declared track owns any path this packet touches -- all seven were checked against every owns: glob in docs/governance/ACTIVE_TRACK.yaml and came back unowned. organism-rewire-2026-07 is named because its charter is 'dormant organs to production' and giving the apex seat memory is exactly that; it serves substrate-nativeness. This packet claims NONE of that track's owned surfaces -- notably not docker-compose.yml or Dockerfile.swarm, which remain its property and are untouched here.

build_plan does NOT condition on memory. Recall reaches the plan input and the operator brief; the planner stays the pure deterministic function its docstring documents. Planning FROM recall has its own gate implications and is deliberately not in this packet.
No container. docker-compose.yml still has no sarathi service, and that file is owned by organism-rewire-2026-07, so it needs that track or a host defined outside it. Not attempted here.

tests/test_holon_system_imports.py fails in the authoring container only: textual>=0.40 is a CORE dependency (pyproject.toml:23) that CI installs via '.[dev]' and the container lacks. Verified to fail identically on clean main with this branch stashed. Unrelated to this change; no repair attempted.
